<header>The Way of Life: A Rebuke of Morality</header>

**And now**, here the sixteen sections are completed, according to their number and their order. In his wisdom, the Sages of the Talmud taught that one should believe only the good of them. And now, after these sections—short and long—we come to the interpretation, like the season of the Creator of light. I will turn my hand to the laws mentioned above in the verse, for "this as well as that" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14; here interpreted as the balance between the sections and the laws of the shofar</note> I have made, with the help of Heaven, to explain them according to the intention of the sections mentioned shortly. The general intention is one: to teach sinners the way, according to the measure of the sections mentioned, both short and long.

## The law is that the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is commanded to be of a ram, etc., according to what is mentioned in the <term>Chatzot Ha-Yom</term> <gloss>The Midday Sections</gloss>, that it is called the "shofar of the penitent" because of the two reasons mentioned there. It seems to me:

<margin>This is called a complete penitent, as the Sages said (in the last chapter of Yoma): What is a complete penitent? For instance, one to whom an opportunity for transgression comes a first, second, and third time, and he is free from it in that specific period (this is the strength of youth), and with that same woman, and in that same place (this is the strength of the transgression). Therefore, their intent in this is his youth and his vigor; he is not exempt from the transgression due to old age or weakness, but rather he is a hero who conquers his inclination and separates—their intent is in this.</margin>
The intent of the Sages in what they said here, "a shofar of Rosh Hashanah" (calling it a shofar of Rosh Hashanah because it is the appointed time of the year to grasp one's deeds and return to the Lord, because repentance preceded Rosh Hashanah for the first man, as mentioned above; and see that Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of the Ten Days of Repentance, so it is appropriate to compare the penitent to the shofar of Rosh Hashanah), its commandment is to be of a ram. The essence of the commandment of a penitent is when he returns from his evil way, that he should return in the days of his youth in his strength and his vigor. The ram mentioned here is from the expression "a ram that butts," and the expression "and he took the rams of the land," and from the expression "it is in the power of my hand," which means it is all strength and vigor. They hinted at the strength of the faculties, and also at the strength of the transgression, meaning that the same transgression in which he stumbled in his youth is prepared before him, and he desires it, and it is within his power to do it as before, yet he is a hero to conquer his inclination and separates from it because of repentance, not because of a loss of strength, for all is exactly the same; his inclination overcomes him and says to him, "Let us do it this time," and he rises and answers, "What I have already done is enough."

## And it seems to me
That this is what they intended by what they interpreted regarding the verse, "Happy is the man who fears the Lord" (Psalm 112:1), and it was brought above in the section on the <term>tzadik</term> <gloss>righteous one</gloss>: "A man, and not a woman." Rav Amram said, "Happy is he who does repentance when he is a 'man' (a young, vigorous person)." And everyone says "happy" when he overcomes his inclination as a man. And Rashi explained, "When he is a fire," at the time when his inclination burns within him, meaning he hastens to extinguish it, or he came before the days of old age as a strong man. And it is possible that Rav did not come to disagree with Rav Amram, but to explain his words. He said that what Rav meant, "Happy is he who does repentance when he is a man," means when he is a youth as mentioned. He did not speak of the strength of the faculties alone, but spoke of the strength of the transgression, that it is as if before him like a burning fire, and he is not in this because of compulsion, but because of the fear of God. He is not a man who runs after his inclination as at the beginning, and he is a hero who conquers his inclination because of the fear of sin. This is what Rav meant, "that he overcomes his inclination, etc." On this, it is fitting to say of him, "Happy is the man who fears the Lord," a complete penitent. And the Rav who said "when he is a man," by which he meant in youth, said "happy is the man," seeing in him two strengths: the strength of youth and the strength of conquering his inclination at that time, with that same woman, etc. This whole principle is hinted at in the word "ram" (ail), which is a word of intensity and strength. There is an additional virtue in this: the strength of the ram regarding the faculties, and the strength of the man regarding the transgression itself at that same time and with that same woman, etc. (Since they are equal, both will come and settle in place). And even if he bows his desire in this, according to our way, the penitent must humble himself and be bowed, to bow his pride and his arrogance, and to cast his soul like dust for all to walk upon. This is the essence of repentance, as above in the section on the <term>dalet</term> <gloss>fourth section</gloss>. The Sages came to inform us here by saying, "a shofar of Rosh Hashanah, its commandment is of a ram." And "bowed," that he should cast down the commandment of the shofar and the action, so that the penitent (likened to the shofar) may reach the highest level for the World to Come. This is that which we are commanded regarding a ram and a bowed [shofar], in the manner mentioned shortly.

### And in the measure
Of the penitent, the repentance of those who have restrained themselves will reach a level of greatness, more fundamental than that which is for the completely righteous who cannot stand in that great place, as mentioned in the section on the <term>nun</term> <gloss>fiftieth section</gloss>. And this is how the penitent reaches such a high level, only lower than him. And it is already explained in the section on the <term>aleph</term> <gloss>first section</gloss> that our level is the World to Come and above it. And it is also explained in the section on the <term>gimel</term> <gloss>third section</gloss> that the level of one penitent is greater and higher in the World to Come than the level of another penitent.

## And this is what is meant by "and after the fact, all shofars are valid, whether straight or bent"
Meaning, even if it is not of a ram and is not bent. And what is meant by "of a ram" according to our way, is that even one who does not repent in his youth when he is in his strength and vigor, which is the superior repentance as above, but waited to repent until his old age—meaning the strength of the vigor of youth and also the strength of the transgression have passed and gone—meaning that the same transgression, period, place, and woman are not prepared before him as before. And what is meant by "bent," is that he also does not humble himself, because to bow his pride to that hard pride, and to be completely lowly as above in the section on the <term>dalet</term> <gloss>fourth section</gloss>, only he removed from himself the pride and spirit, and also the excessive pride that he had beforehand, which brought him to sin as it is said, "And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget the Lord your God." He stands now in this at the midpoint of humility, and has not humbled himself entirely, and he has a level in the World to Come, and this is the fifth level mentioned in the section on the <term>gimel</term> <gloss>third section</gloss>. This is what is said, "and after the fact all shofars are valid." And this is what seems to me to be what the Sages intended regarding the law of the ram and the bent [shofar]. According to our way, in addition to what we said above: "Prepare before Me a shofar of a ram, so that I may remember for you the Binding of Isaac, and that I may raise you up as if you had bound yourselves before Me," and "bent" so that they may bend their hearts to prayer.

# And they said, "except for that of a cow, which is disqualified in any case"
And its interpretation: if it is from a cow, even after the fact, it is disqualified. The Sages hinted here, according to our way, at those people who resemble the red heifer, which is colored by the redness of sin. And if they grow red due to transgressions even until old age and hoariness, they do not repent, or they do not repent because of pride and loftiness of spirit, for every proud person refrains from repenting, because repentance depends on humility as mentioned in the section on the <term>nun</term> <gloss>fiftieth section</gloss>. And it is said regarding Ahab, "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me?" etc.

## And this is what is meant
(And it is not named in the Holy Tongue a *shofar* but a *horn*) because you know that the word "horn" is authority, as in "My horn is exalted," and also "the horn of His anointed," "the horn of salvation." It means one who has not abandoned pride and authority, therefore he does not set his heart to repent, as it is said, "And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget the Lord your God," etc. Therefore, it is disqualified even after the fact if it is a horn of pride, because pride does not allow him to repent, as above. These are those of whom the Sages said (in the chapter "They make fences"), "The wicked, even at the gate of Gehinnom, do not repent," and they die in their sin due to the horns of their pride.

## And they said, "because"
And likewise the horns of most beasts, meaning wild, predatory beasts. These are the wicked, who are like the beasts of the forest as is seen in the chapter "The Useful." They are one essence, meaning they do not have a heart of flesh, but a heart of stone and bone, and they harden their hearts from repenting all their days, forever, until they die in their sins.

## And this is what is meant
And their shofar is bent backwards—meaning they do not remember in the inner parts of their hearts the day of death, and they are not fearful, and they are not worried, and they are not saddened by it. Just as the Sages said (in tractate Shabbat) on the verse, "There are no bands for their death," the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "It is not enough for the wicked that they are not fearful and saddened by the day of death, but their hearts are healthy to them as a hall," etc. Therefore, they are disqualified completely in the World to Come (as this shofar is disqualified even after the fact), and they are the *epikoros* <gloss>heretics/skeptics</gloss> who do not believe in the Day of Judgment and the providence over his body and soul to punish, and they are given between them for generations, as mentioned at the end of the section on the <term>gimel</term> <gloss>third section</gloss>.

# "All sounds are valid in the shofar"
Meaning the corrections of the sounds. These sounds, meaning even if one says, "In all the Torah, the Lord will calculate in His mercy, even if I have done many transgressions, what will the performance of the commandment help me if I have done many sins and performed many commandments?" for it is said, "For by strategies you shall wage your war." And the Sages interpreted regarding this, a person whose sins are piled up, [the commandments] will be done against them as sounds.

Herewith, the sixteenth section concludes, as numbered and as ordained. In His wisdom, the Sages of the Talmud said: "They shall believe nothing from them but the good." Now, after these sections—short and long—we come to the interpretation, as at the season of the Creator of Light. I will turn my hand to the laws mentioned above in the verse, "For this against that" <note>Ecclesiastes 7:14; here interpreted as the balance between the various sections and the laws of the Shofar</note>, for I have done so with the help of Heaven to explain them according to the inner intent of the sections mentioned shortly. The general intent is one: "He instructs sinners in the way," according to the value of the sections mentioned, both short and long.

## The Law is that the Shofar of Rosh Hashanah is commanded to be of a ram, etc., according to what is mentioned in the section <note>This refers to an earlier part of the text, "Chatzat Ha-Yediot"</note>, as it is called the "Shofar of the Penitent" by virtue of the two reasons mentioned there. It appears to me:

<margin>This is called a "complete penitent," as the Sages said (in the final chapter of Yoma): What is a complete penitent? For example, when a forbidden thing comes into his hand a first, second, and third time, and he is exempt from it during that period (this is the strength of youth), and with the same woman, and in the same place (this is the strength of the sin). Therefore, they meant by this, during his youth and his sharpness, and he is not exempted from the sin due to old age or weakness of strength, but he is a hero in conquering his inclination and refrains from it.</margin>

The intention of the Sages in saying here "the Shofar of Rosh Hashanah" (and calling it the Shofar of Rosh Hashanah because it is the appointed time of the year to examine one's deeds and return to God, for repentance preceded the creation of man, as mentioned above, and see that Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of the Ten Days of Repentance, so it is appropriate to compare the penitent to the Shofar of Rosh Hashanah) is that it is commanded to be of a ram. For the essence of the duty of the penitent is that when he turns from his evil way, he should turn in the days of his youth, in his strength and power. And the "ram" mentioned here is from the expression "a ram that butts," and "he took the rams of the land," and from the expression "it is in the power <term>el</term> <gloss>strength/god</gloss> of my hand," meaning all of them are strength and power. They hinted at the strength of the powers, and also at the "strength of the sin." That is to say, that same sin in which he stumbled in his youth is presented before him, and he desires it, and it is in his power to do it as before, yet he is a hero in conquering his inclination and refrains from it because of repentance, not because of a failure of strength. For it is similar in every respect to when his inclination overcomes him and says to him, "Let us do it as we did that time," and he stands up and refuses what he has already done.

## And it appears to me
That this is what they intended by what they interpreted regarding the verse, "Happy is the man who fears the Lord" (Psalm 112:1). It was brought above in the section: "A man, and not a woman." Rav Amram said: "Happy is he who does repentance when he is a man <term>ish</term> <gloss>adult/man/strength</gloss>." Everyone says "happy" when he overcomes his inclination as a man. Rashi explained: "When he is fire <term>esh</term> <gloss>fire</gloss>, at the time when it burns with heat," meaning he hastens to extinguish it, or he came before the days of old age as a strong man. It is possible that Rav Amram did not come to disagree with Rav, but to explain the words of Rav. He said that what Rav meant—"Happy is he who does repentance when he is a man"—is that he meant when he is a youth, as mentioned. He did not speak only of the strength of his powers, but he spoke of the "strength of the sin," that it is similar to the fires of desire, and he is not in this because of compulsion but because of God, and he is not a body driven to chase after his inclination as at the beginning, but he is a hero who conquers his inclination because of the fear of sin. This is what Rav Amram said: "who overcomes his inclination," etc. For this, it is appropriate to say of him "Happy is the man who fears the Lord," a complete penitent. And Rav, who said "when he is a man," meaning youth, said "Happy is the man" because he possesses two strengths: the strength of youth and the strength of conquering his inclination in that time, with that woman, etc. This whole principle is hinted at in the word "ram," which is a term for strength and power. There is additional praise in this: the strength of the "ram" in terms of youth, and the strength of the "man" in terms of the sin itself at that time, with that woman, etc. (Since they are equal, both may be brought). Even if he bends his will, according to our way, the penitent needs to humble himself and be bowed, to bend his pride and arrogance, and his pride should be as dust to all. This is the essence of repentance, as mentioned above in the section. The Sages came to inform us here by saying, "The Shofar of Rosh Hashanah, its commandment is of a ram," and "bent," that he should cast down his pride, and the action of the Shofar is that the penitent (likened to the Shofar) will arrive at the highest level for the World to Come. This is that we are commanded concerning a ram and a bent one, according to the way mentioned shortly.

### And in the measure
Of the penitent, the repentance that he forces himself to perform will bring him to a level of great importance, so much so that "perfect righteous ones cannot stand in the place where penitents stand," as mentioned in the section. And this is why the penitent reaches such a great level, though he is lower than them. It is already explained in the section that our level is the World to Come and above it, and it is also explained in the section that the level of one penitent is greater and higher in the World to Come than the level of another penitent.

## And this is what is meant by "In any case, all Shofars are valid, whether straight or bent"
Meaning, even if it is not of a ram and is not bent. And I mean "of a ram" according to our way, that is, even he who does not repent in his youth when he is in his strength and power, which is the superior repentance as mentioned above, but waited to repent until his old age—meaning the strength of the power of youth and the power of the sin has passed and gone. Meaning, that same sin—time, place, and woman—is not presented before him as before. And I mean "bent" that he is also not subdued enough to bend his pride, to break that difficult pride to complete humility as mentioned in the section, but he removed from himself the pride of spirit and the excessive pride that was in him previously, which led him to sin, as it is written: "And your heart will be haughty and you will forget the Lord your God." He now stands on the middle ground of humility, and he has not humbled himself to the first degree, but he has the quality of repentance and he has some level in the World to Come. This is the fifth level mentioned in the section. This is what it means, "In any case, all Shofars are valid." And it appears to me that this is what the Sages intended in the law of the ram and the bent one, according to our way. Added to what we said: "Prepare before Me a Shofar of a ram, so that I may remember for you the Binding of Isaac, and I will account it for you as if you bound yourselves before Me," and "bent" so that they may bend themselves for prayer.

# And they said: Except for that of a cow, which is disqualified in any case
Its explanation is: If it is of a cow, even in any case, it is disqualified. The Sages hinted here, according to our way, at those people who are like the Red Heifer, which is called by the redness of sin. And if they remain red—as it were—due to sins even until old age and hoary hair, they do not repent, or they do not repent because of pride and haughtiness of spirit, for in every haughty heart it is difficult to do repentance, because repentance depends on submission, as mentioned in the section. And it is said regarding Ahab: "Have you seen how Ahab humbled himself before Me," etc.

## And this is what is meant
(And it is not called in the Holy Tongue a Shofar but a Horn <term>Keren</term> <gloss>horn/power</gloss>). Since you have already known that the term "horn" is authority, as in "My horn is exalted," and also "the horn of His anointed," "the horn of salvation," and it means that he has not abandoned pride and authority, therefore he does not set his heart to return, as it is written: "And your heart will be haughty and you will forget the Lord your God," etc. Therefore, it is disqualified even in any case if it is a "horn of pride." For pride does not let him repent as mentioned above. And these are those of whom the Sages said (in the chapter *Osin Pasin*): "The wicked, even at the entrance of Gehinnom, do not repent," and they died in their sin by the power of their horns of pride.

## And they said "because"
Also the horns of most animals, meaning wild, predatory beasts. These are the wicked who are like the beasts of the forest, as seen in the relevant chapter. They are "one bone," meaning they have no heart of flesh but a heart of stone and bone, and they harden their hearts from doing repentance all their days forever, until they die in their sins.

## And this is what is meant
"And their 'bent' <term>kefufim</term> <gloss>bent/those who bow</gloss> are remembered," meaning that they do not remember in the depths of their hearts the day of death, and they do not tremble, and they do not worry, and they are not saddened by it. Like the Sages (in tractate Shabbat) on the verse, "There are no bands <term>chartzubot</term> <gloss>bonds/pangs</gloss> for their death." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "It is not enough for the wicked that they do not tremble and worry about the day of death, but their heart is healthy for them as a ram..." etc. Therefore, they are disqualified entirely for the World to Come (just as this Shofar is disqualified even in any case). And they are the Epicureans <term>apikorsim</term> <gloss>heretics</gloss> who do not believe in the Day of Judgment and the providence of his body and soul to punish, and he is placed among them for generations of generations, as mentioned at the end of the section.

# All sounds are valid in the Shofar
Meaning, the corrections of the sounds. These are the sounds, meaning even if he has sinned in the entire Torah, the Lord will consider it in His mercy, even if he has done many sins. And what will the performance of a commandment avail me if I have done many sins and done many commandments? For it is said: "For by strategies you shall wage your war," and the Sages interpreted this: "A man whose sins have accumulated, let him do against them the sounds."

The powerful force, even though it possesses the power to perform a certain thing on its own, yet the chosen entity receives from it a measure of perfection. And this, too, is complete joy. This is among the difficult matters; indeed, this joy is of the perfection related to the reward, and it is great. This is what it is.

There are beings that possess an absolutely great soul, and the divine intellect is emanated within them. This power is found in an intellect that is deeper than all else and precise. This intellect is also found to contain the supernal form, which is emanated from the simple hidden source, which flows from the first, absolute, blessed source. This form is a noble form, and it possesses permanence because it is a fixed matter in the human heart. This noble and exalted intellect is found in the heart, and the eminence is in the simple intellect within the holy, singular heart. Since the matter is not from itself but is emanated from the mouth of the supernal Name, may He be blessed, it is the exalted being. The eminence is that which man shares with the whole; the form is the absolute form. From the matter within it, which is the divine being, it is emanated from this emanated intellect, which is emanated from the Name, may He be blessed, which is the absolute source. The matter is found in the human heart, which is termed this supernal intellect, and it is of the great eminence that is given to Him, may the Name be blessed. "How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You" <note>Psalm 31:20</note> is written concerning the righteous. This verse gives us a hint of the reward for the good and these righteous deeds. This gift is a fire that consumes the reward, and the joy appears from Him, may He be blessed. This eminence is the happiness, and it is a spiritual good that the King establishes, a spiritual radiance of emanation in the heart of the noble intellect. The desire is the tranquility for man. Thus, the intellect is the whole, as from the foundation, it is the essence within it, which is the exalted being regarding the soul and the spirit that has entered the body. Thus, it has an eminence.

In the Torah, there are many degrees, and two simple matters in the supernal degree are written, and it is known. The sign for this is the verse "Go up to God" <note>Exodus 24:1</note>. This is the degree. This level elevates the degree above the supernal sea that is in the soul, the spiritual eminence that is in the intellect. It is not fitting for a person to find himself in this degree while it is in the heart like jealousy, and it shall be a small heel acting as a cow <note>Interpretation of Rashi’s commentary on "Bikar" (Firstborn)</note> for this. This matter is a cow over his intellect, and the firstborn son of which Rashi, of blessed memory, wrote in the language of the passage. The intellect that shone upon them comes to the illuminated heart, and it said, "The light of my priest" <note>Referring to the light of the intellect/understanding</note>. One will not find this absolute pleasure, for the birthright is the supernal degree to learn and understand in the Torah and in everything. "He has much knowledge" <note>Refers to intellectual capacity</note>. Thus, the wealth acts as a cow for this, and the intellect acts as a cow over his intellect. It is of the supernal degree that is in the house, and he was walking, and after him was the blessing of the work of his hands. This degree, we have said, the being exalted over his intellect, is a great eminence. The degree is a wondrous eminence, more than that of any level of the wise, as it is written, "The loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>mercy/loving-kindness</gloss> of the Name is from everlasting to everlasting." "Thus to the loving-kindness of the Name, may He be blessed, shall it fill thus."

In this matter, one is found on the level in the most exalted eminence. The supernal being is the exalted messenger that receives the divine guidance. This kingdom <term>Malkhut</term> <gloss>Kingship/Kingdom</gloss> is a great and vast eminence, the exalted level enumerated in the verse "For Yours is the honor and the greatness, for everything is from You" <note>1 Chronicles 29:11</note>, in the eminence given by the noble intellect. It is not given from the eighth degree, as it is in the verse that holiness is given. The sign for this is "Everything is praise," and this is the secret of the wonder. It is said that this gift is over everything, and the heart is not a power over it from the intellect. The pure and noble heart is from the supernal degree termed the eminence of the intellect, which cannot be measured by the intellect of men. "Behold, You desire truth in the innermost parts" <note>Psalm 51:6</note>, for one cannot find this absolute heart in reward and in Torah. In this, the absolute will be found, following this in the day with the power of intellect and contemplation. For this joy is not here in a great eminence, and the supernal being is in the degree termed holy, refined, pure, and clean. Since the reward and the gift from the simple intellect are given to the distributor of loving-kindness, which awakens the blessing and is in the measure of charity toward the creatures, the relation is according to the wealth of the eminence. This is the gift in the measure of the foundation <term>Yesod</term> <gloss>foundation</gloss> for the noble Name from this supernal degree. One finds success and the absolute intellect in the human heart in all matters, so that he does not sin in his heart. The mighty sign is "For He desires loving-kindness." Thus, the absolute intellect is found above in the heart of the servant, the secret of the foundation of the Name in his absolute divine soul, the foundation of the spirit and the soul that walks on the path of the eminence in the elevation. Likewise, the matter of the kingdom is mercy in perfection. The kingdom and the loving-kindness within it, the supernal eminence, are given by the power of intellect and contemplation within the receiving divine intellect, and it shall lead and leads according to the eminence in the aspect. It was, as he aspires to the noble intellect and the simple, exalted, noble heart, and all is in the providence which they found from the excellent reward upon the heart, and he lives in the life of this perfection. This essential eminence comes with joy, and the holy, pious heart, from the mouth of this eminence which is explained in the language of the Scripture, is this intellect. The days of Jacob drew near to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him: "If I have now found favor in your eyes, place now your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and truth; do not bury me in Egypt. I will lie with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place." And he said: "I will do as you have spoken." He said: "Swear to me," and he swore to him, and Israel bowed upon the head of the bed.

It came to pass after these things that someone said to Joseph: "Behold, your father is ill." He took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim. It was told to Jacob, and he said: "Behold, your son Joseph comes to you," and Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed. Jacob said to Joseph: "God Almighty <term>El Shaddai</term> <gloss>a name of God associated with divine protection and fertility</gloss> appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me. "And now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you to Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine as Reuben and Simeon are. Your offspring whom you beget after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance. As for me, when I came from Padan, Rachel died upon me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was yet but a distance of land to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, the same is Bethlehem."

One who deposits items with his friend, whether money or produce, and says to him, "Here is my deposit," and he says to him, "Hide it," and he did not know where he placed the deposit or in which place he placed the funds, "Wait for me until I return," and he says to him, "You were negligent," and he brings upon him his property and the property of the deposit, and the body of the items, all of them to be held as a pledge, and if he was exempt for doing so and they did not know, he is exempt from everything. 8. If he was told to hide it, and he did so without pay, he is exempt. 9. If he was told to hide it and he did not hide it properly, and he placed it in a dangerous area and it died in its normal manner, he is exempt. If, however, its beginning was through negligence, he would be liable, and even if it was torn or damaged, he would be liable. Regarding the way of storage: There is a deposit whose way of storage is like bundles of grain or bundles of beams or wood, and there is a deposit whose way of storage is to place it in a sack, like bundles of clothes or a cloak. ## Liturgical Poem for the Sabbath of Shekalim

**BLESSED** are You, O Lord our God, King of the universe, who forms light and creates darkness, who makes peace and creates all things. Eternal light in the treasury of life, lights from darkness, He spoke and it came to be.
God who is exalted over all as the Head. He chose the nation that was downtrodden in its status as head <note>a reference to Israel's humble beginnings or minority status</note>. Like the first fruit of the fig tree at its beginning, He coaxed God and sought it out, to separate it from all nations, to lift it above every head. He shall turn the despised one toward the terror of the head, and it shall lift its head, upon the throne of glory from the beginning.
My Redeemer and lifter of my head. Now may He pass over my head. And He shall inquire and seek, Holy One.
He spoke in this book, and established with words of beauty, for those who rule from dust and ashes, that they should give a ransom, without blemish or shame, to atone for their iniquity, and their righteousness shall be written in a book.
In the memory of the book, for their standing, and also I, who am dust and ashes. This is our God, the visionary for my father, and they showed him a kind of coin of fire in a vision. And also, all shall prophesy through this. He shall bestow kindnesses in this, and after them, where shall they build and where shall Judah gather them, and they shall sit in goodness upon this. And they shall be able to see the Divine Presence, and a nation shall trample nation, he shall sprinkle. The Unique One who dwells in the heights, graced it with the perfect Torah. To the dove that is pure, all who pass through it, they shall weigh a shekel without turmoil, a half-shekel as a contribution, for their benefit without opposition, and it shall be a wall for her, who hangs the earth upon nothingness. From twenty years of age they shall volunteer with song, the face of the Dweller of the dwelling, leaders and ways with support. All shall be equal in giving, without delay, forever and around supplication, at all times and at every season. And they shall endure with song, upon their souls an atonement, and they shall redeem their sin and good shall be divided. They shall improve Aram, all shall recount, and they shall offer praise and complete it, and they shall sing thanksgiving to the Rock. Their enemies shall be diminished and straightened, and upon their necks they shall prevail, and in abundance of joys they shall be blessed.
Their congregation to strengthen themselves in the Torah, without further curse, as they approach this to idolatry, with them He gathered in love and desire, in salvation and in establishment, their name in the life that is perpetual, in all that is included in the praise, and for me without service it shall always be a memorial to the Rose of Sharon, in atonement and advantage, before the High One, Holy. All shall thank You.
You loved Your people on account of generation after generation from the heights. You magnified Your name for them, You caused them to cleave to the love of Your name. They are Your inheritance and Your people, and they are persistent in exalting You, and He shall remember the covenant of those who speak for You. Pity and bring near their day for them. You gave good to the mighty, they weighed silver as atonement, as a ransom for iniquity they make atonement, forever they shall be guarded. From the age of the commandment of twenty, the giving of the poor and the rich, the handful of all that are counted, upon their banner in all borders, they have recorded them and their names.

What have you seen and what have you heard from our mouth, and what greatness is this, to forgive one who has sinned? 
Furthermore, one must know, what is this "with kindness"? For since you knew that your fear <note>i.e., the fear of God</note> would be upon them, because by forgiving the one who sinned, they will fear you and fear lest they sin against you, lest you punish them according to their sin instead of forgiving them upon seeing their repentance. This kindness will return, especially in this forgiveness, for they sinned with the <term>Egel</term> <gloss>the Golden Calf</gloss>, and He forgave them and punished them little by little. This is what is meant by "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children," as Rashi explains on the verse regarding the visiting of the iniquity of the fathers upon the children. Similarly, in Psalm 131, regarding the verse "For with You is forgiveness, that You may be feared" <note>Psalm 130:4</note>. For by the law and judgment of God, there should be punishment, and through forgiveness and pardon, doubt is strengthened in the sinner that perhaps, through repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive him. 

From this, he is strengthened to return in repentance and fears lest he return to his folly and fears sin. From this, he is stirred, for when the wicked see that He is compassionate when they see they must repent, they will see within themselves that their transgressions are many and that they have sinned against the great and awesome Name. Through this, they will fear the Name, and He will be moved over their sin when they perform repentance. Through the forgiveness granted to them on account of their fear, the kindness will return to them if they are constant in their fear. And this is: "The kindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him" <note>Psalm 103:17</note>. 

The meaning of "from everlasting to everlasting" is according to its measure, according to the ten attributes with which the world was created. Therefore, they are in forgiveness after their sin, not in a general way, but specifically according to their repentance and their fear, so that it will be in their seeing the greatness of God's power, the greatness of His eminence, His goodness, and His kindness, meaning instead of punishing them for what they sinned in that matter. And "His righteousness to children's children," meaning through God's kindness, He visits them with forgiveness and kindness, as Rashi explains in the portion of <term>Ki Tissa</term> <gloss>When you take [the sum]</gloss>. And "His righteousness," meaning the kindness He shared with them, for through righteousness He acted with them, for He had compassion on them. This kindness will return to them, for He visits their iniquities upon them little by little, for you knew to pass over them with kindness and forgiveness, and they will fear God through the forgiveness. For in seeing this constantly, they will fear God, and this is the kindness of the Lord, for it will return to them from everlasting to everlasting. And this is the kindness of the Lord and His righteousness to children's children, so that they might bear the iniquities of their fathers. And this is what the Scripture says: "And the kindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting."

At the end of the first chapter of <term>Rosh Hashanah</term> <gloss>the Jewish New Year</gloss>, Rav Judah said: A covenant was made for the thirteen attributes that they do not return empty, as it is said: "Behold, I make a covenant," etc. And one must know, what kindness is there here in this covenant? In their seeing that the kindness of the Lord and His righteousness to children's children visit their iniquities upon them, and this is a covenant that was made. What have you seen and what have you heard from us, and how great is this, to forgive those who have sinned? 

One must also know what this <term>chesed</term> <gloss>loving-kindness/grace</gloss> is. For you know that this implies that your fear <note>i.e., the fear of God</note> will be upon them. For when you forgive those who have sinned, they will fear you and dread lest they sin against you, fearing that you might punish them according to their sin instead of forgiving them. When they see this grace, it returns <note>to them</note>, especially in this forgiveness for those who sinned with the golden calf. They were forgiven, yet He punished them little by little. This is the meaning of "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children," as <term>Rashi</term> <gloss>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki, the prominent medieval commentator</gloss> explains on the verse. Similarly, in Psalm 103, it says, "But with You is forgiveness, that You may be feared." For by the law and judgment of God, there should be punishment, but through pardon and forgiveness, a doubt is strengthened in the sinner—perhaps, through repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive him. 

Because of this, he is strengthened to return in repentance, and he fears lest he return to his old ways, and he fears the sin. From this, he is stirred, for when the wicked see compassion upon their return in repentance, they see within themselves how great their transgressions are and that they have sinned against the Great and Awesome Name. Through this, they fear God, who is reconciled to their sin when they repent. Through the forgiveness granted to them on account of their fear, the grace returns to them, provided they remain in constant fear. This is "the grace of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him." 

The interpretation of "from everlasting to everlasting" is according to its measure, according to the thirteen attributes by which the world was created. Therefore, they are granted forgiveness after their sin, not in a general way but specifically according to their repentance and their fear, so that when they see the greatness of God’s power, the greatness of His eminence, His goodness, and His grace, they will fear Him rather than continuing in the matter of their sin. "And His righteousness to children’s children" means that through the grace of God, He visits their iniquities upon them by means of forgiveness and grace, as <term>Rashi</term> explains in the Torah portion <term>Ki Tissa</term> <gloss>Exodus 30:11-34:35</gloss>. "And His righteousness"—this refers to the grace He shared with them, for He acted toward them with righteousness because He had compassion on them. This grace returns to them, for He visits their iniquities upon them little by little, because He knows how to pass over transgressions with grace and forgiveness. They fear God through this forgiveness, for when they see this constantly, they will fear God. This is the grace of the Lord, for it returns to them from everlasting to everlasting. This is the "grace of the Lord and His righteousness to children’s children," so that they might endure the iniquities of their fathers. This is what the Scripture means when it says, "And the grace of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting."

At the end of the first chapter of <term>Rosh Hashanah</term> <gloss>the Jewish New Year</gloss>, <term>Rav Yehuda</term> <gloss>a prominent Talmudic sage</gloss> said: A covenant was made regarding the thirteen attributes that they do not return empty, as it is said, "Behold, I make a covenant," etc. One must know what grace is present here in this covenant. When they see that the grace of the Lord and His righteousness are upon children’s children, and He visits their iniquities upon them, this is the "covenant that was made." This covenant and this grace come through the thirteen attributes by which the world was created. The Lord created the world with grace and with the attribute of mercy. Through these thirteen attributes, mercy and grace are stirred, for as they were at the creation, "In the beginning God created," etc. Through these thirteen attributes, the grace of the Lord is stirred from everlasting to everlasting, and "His righteousness to children’s children." His righteousness and His grace return to them through the merit of the fathers and through the thirteen attributes by which the world was created. This is the "grace of the Lord from everlasting to everlasting."

Its mystery is that which I will return to, in the mystery of the first [day] and the firmament, and as it is with the beginning of "Let there be light, let there be a firmament, let there be lights," our Father in light, and "let there be light for a living soul," our Father in deep language regarding the Work of Creation in the firmament, and as it is with the creatures of the earth, and our Father in the essence of the Name. Our Father in the language of creation <term>Beriah</term> <gloss>the world of Creation</gloss>, as in the Work of Creation and in the light, "And God called the light [Day]," in its revelation, our Father as creatures, and elevating it over everything. In all of this, the language of formation <term>Yetzirah</term> <gloss>the world of Formation</gloss> was not mentioned. However, regarding the saying, "And the Lord God formed <term>va-yitzer</term> <gloss>formed (from the root Y-T-Z-R)</gloss> man," and what is written, "And the Lord God formed out of the ground every beast of the field, etc.," they have already said in *Genesis Rabbah* Chapter 17 that it was for the sake of subduing and overpowering [the material] from the substance <note>The root *Yetzirah* is here linked to the act of conquering or shaping raw matter</note>. "And He formed" is a language of subduing. The reason seems to be that the entire Work of Creation is structured and proceeds according to these souls, which are like the work of the covenant <note>referring to the covenant of circumcision or the righteous</note>, if not for "day and night, etc." <note>A reference to the verse in Jeremiah 33:25 regarding the ordinances of heaven and earth</note>. And they fear from Him, the sea and the foundation of the earth, creating worlds and depicting them according to their value, and good deeds are its initial light. For in its depth, it is always in the sons, God acquires Torah and teaches in every statute if it adds and renews in the work of the Torah and its attributes. And the foundation is in it, in the language of formation <term>Yetzirah</term>, to... its master, recognize it in the *Midrash* of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, regarding what is written: "Everyone that is called by My name, and for My glory I have created him, I have formed him, yea, I have made him." <note>Isaiah 43:7</note> Because the supreme glory has within it the covenant of creation, formation, and making. However, it was created for the rectification of the Glory, and for this reason, these languages were included in it, as was explained in Chapter 17 of the first part of this book in the name of... in all the created beings... the purpose. And therefore, the language of formation did not come in the name of... [this] certain one, [Rabbi] wise man to teach it by what he said, that he is this, etc., to equate it to the rest of the created beings in that it is without limitation. And with you as well, they will say not in it... the time of success to increase in the status of the righteous and the chosen. For all created beings are vessels and are rectified, they are joined to him. For according to Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi... we can say that the created beings are in relation to the righteous as the ministers to the king, for they are the ones who are organized and the deeds for the king, a band of ministers, were created to serve them in his kingdom, and his changing, and his kingdom. And it is proper to... for the nations, all of this is... much from the virtues of the Torah. And this is to create, for all created beings are in perfection, joined to the righteous, even in the rectification of his food and drink, as is known the virtues of the righteous and the generations in the honor of the <term>sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss> and the connections. And it is written of them: "And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth," in the verse that is written... in the words of Nahmanides <note>Ramban</note>, of blessed memory, who wrote in Chapter 23 of this, at the end of the passage... and the end, they said regarding the stars, "to give light upon the space," and from this it was written... in order to benefit through that... to recognize the reason that it adhered... that is to say, "lights" <term>me'orot</term> <gloss>luminaries</gloss> from... as it was said regarding man, "and have dominion over the fish of the sea." What is its matter that it was spoken for this, only to return... which is the intent... also to say that the created beings all came for the benefit of the righteous and for his utility and his aid. And what is written, "to give light, etc.," all is to give light, a claim, and to strengthen the claim that is intended in the world... for the good of the world, until they are in their essence in reason and understanding that the faith is for this, that is to say, to be man. And so wrote our Sages, of blessed memory... and added more in the chapter of the *Kuzari*. And this said, the whole world was not created but to serve this... in connection... and his creation for this, his blessings without... all

that which is... and the rectification for his existence, so that he may be always free and ready for the Supreme Life and the rectification of the Glory. This... was the goal of his purpose. And our Sages, of blessed memory, have already said in the *Sifrei* that the upper ones were created to serve the lower ones. These... Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, the apple of the heel of the first man would eclipse the globe of the sun. And do not be surprised... in the star that is in the world... of the disk, he said to him, and since it is so, whose work is he doing? He is doing it for himself. And he who has understanding will see that it is not that the righteous are intended for themselves, for all the works, for it is not for themselves they were born. And the statement, "The globe of the sun for the service of the creatures," is evidence that it is not according to the words of the Rabbi who said that they are intended for themselves, and it is in his power... and the <term>sefirot</term> <gloss>divine emanations</gloss> until he was elevated. Those believers who remain at home, other than those who suffer from a disability, are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their persons. God has given those who strive with their wealth and their persons a rank above those who remain at home. Yet to both, God has promised the best reward. God has favored those who strive over those who remain at home with a great reward, as well as degrees of rank from Him, forgiveness, and mercy. God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. When the angels take the souls of those who have wronged themselves, they ask, "In what state were you?" They reply, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels ask, "Was not God's earth spacious enough for you to migrate within it?" For such people, their abode will be Hell, an evil destination. Excepted are the oppressed among men, women, and children who have no means and cannot find a way. For them, it is hoped that God will pardon them; God is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving. Whoever migrates in the cause of God will find on earth many places of refuge and abundance. Whoever leaves his home, migrating to God and His Messenger, and is then overtaken by death, his reward has already been established with God. God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. When you travel through the land, there is no sin upon you 

<column-break/>

if you shorten your prayers if you fear that those who disbelieve will harm you. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy. When you are among them and stand to lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and take their weapons. When they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group who have not yet prayed come forward and pray with you, and let them take their precautions and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you were heedless of your weapons and your belongings so that they might attack you all at once. There is no sin upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill to lay down your weapons, but take your precautions. God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. When you have finished your prayer, remember God while standing, sitting, or lying on your sides. When you are secure again, establish the prayer, for prayer is prescribed for the believers at specific times. Do not weaken in your pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, they are also suffering as you suffer, but you hope from God for what they do not hope for. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise. We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you.

The believers who remain at home, other than those who are disabled, are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who remain at home by a degree. To each, Allah has promised the best outcome. But Allah has distinguished those who strive over those who remain at home with a great reward: degrees of rank from Him, as well as forgiveness and mercy. Indeed, Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. Indeed, as for those whom the angels take in death while they were wronging themselves, they will ask, "In what condition were you?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and it is an evil destination. Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan and are not guided to a way. It is expected that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning, All-Forgiving. Whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find on the earth many places of refuge and abundance. And whoever leaves his home, emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. from the Companions, it is interpreted as him thinking that this game is not merely for amusement, but is instead intended as a means to learn warfare and develop skill in it. In summary, if it were intended for the purpose of killing and aiding in it, then it would be recommended and encouraged, based on the words of the Almighty: "Prepare for them whatever force you are able to muster." Furthermore, the argument of those who say that it involves the strategy of war is invalid, for it is of no use in war. Even if one were to concede this, it is generally not the intent; the intent is usually play and gambling through wastefulness, which is even more effective at distracting them from the remembrance of God and from prayer. 

As for the person who says—as will come later—that perhaps Ibn Umar was among those who validated the status of <term>nard</term> <gloss>dice/backgammon</gloss> and that he did not do anything wrong, God forbid that Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with both him and his father, would do such a thing, given the overwhelming evidence regarding its prohibition. The Companions were the most committed to following the truth and the most scrupulous in their investigations. Ibn al-Arabi, may God have mercy on him, was excessive in his rejection of chess in his book Al-Qabas <gloss>The Torch/The Brand</gloss>, where he stated: "Al-Shafi'i permitted it," and the state of some reached the point of saying it is recommended, to the extent that they introduced it into schools. Thus, when a student became fatigued from studying, he would play it in the mosque, and they based this on a group of the Companions and the Successors having played it. But that never happened, and by God, no hand of a pious person has ever touched it. 

They say that it sharpens the mind, but direct observation proves them wrong. A man of intelligence never achieves mastery in it. I heard Imam Abu al-Fadl ibn Ata al-Maqdisi say in the Al-Aqsa Mosque during a debate that it teaches war. The Caliph supported the sciences and became the patron of scientists.

After the death of Mūsā bin Shākir, al-Ma'mūn, who cared for the Banū Mūsā brothers, entrusted Isḥāk bin Ibrāhīm with their guardianship. The famous astronomer and astrologer Yaḥyā bin Abī Manṣūr became their tutor. Thus, the Mūsā brothers had the opportunity during their education to study deeply the subjects for which they had talent and interest.

The life of the Banū Mūsā brothers was initially as simple as that of the close circle al-Ma'mūn brought from Marw to Baghdad in 813. However, soon after the death of al-Ma'mūn, their lives became luxurious. The wealth and influence of the brothers grew through the favors of the caliphs and the income streams attributed to them. They devoted much of their wealth to the pursuit of works by ancient writers, sent missions to Byzantium to seek out such material, paid a group of translators to render them into Arabic, and spent great energy on the development of the sciences. This attitude served as a model for others, such as Qusta bin Lūqā. Muḥammed is said to have made a journey to Anatolia for this reason and brought back with him, from Harran to Baghdad, one of the most famous scientists and a renowned translator of Islam, Thābit bin Qurrā. The brothers used to pay about five hundred dinars a month to a group of translators who worked on collected texts in the House of Wisdom <note>original: "Bayt al-Ḥikma"</note>.

The brothers' interest and ability in geometry, ingenious devices, music, and astronomy were not always of the same level. Among them, Abu Ja'far Muḥammed was the most influential; it is said that he knew the works of Euclid and Ptolemy, and that his knowledge in the fields of mathematics, astronomy, logic, and philosophy was extensive. Aḥmed's talent lay in technical matters. The books on the construction of ingenious devices (<term>hiyal</term> <gloss>mechanical stratagems/devices</gloss>) and musical automation must be his work. Ḥasan was a brilliant geometrician. Muḥammed was also highly active in politics. They mostly lived together, remained active during the reigns of various caliphs, and were sociable in the modern sense of the word.

### Al-Thaqqāf: It is stated in <term>Aqrab al-Mawārid</term> <gloss>a modern Arabic dictionary</gloss>: "The *thaqqāf* is a wooden tool used to straighten spears." Regarding this, ʿAmr says:

> When the *thaqqāf* bites into it, it recoils    And turns away, stubborn and rough

Meaning: when the *thaqqāf* takes hold of the spear to straighten it, the spear resists being straightened and turns away. The *thaqqāf* is a hard, strong, and forceful channel.

Their various tastes are all merely the dragging of the imagination. Likewise, the form which is said to be "He," and that the whole is a part of its essence. Likewise, the One that appears as if it were an accident to essence, resembling existence. It is imagined that the Necessary Being <note>original: "al-Wajib"</note> is this, while other things are like the preceding essence, and it is sometimes imagined that it is the Possible Being <note>original: "al-Mumkin"</note>. For anything other than this existence, or for what exists, there is an aspect of its own essence which is pure poverty, and an aspect toward this existence by which it is existent. 

There is no unity in Paradise, nor the unity of its people, nor the unity of him who said: "The court of the Truth is too exalted to be a thoroughfare for every comer." Nor is there the unity of him who said: "No one has unified the One." Nor is there the unity of him who said: "He is not seen except by His light, and He is not witnessed except by His presence." Nor of him who said: "How can He be seen when it is by Him that all is seen?" 

In summary, the One [451] is limited to four types: the one by continuity, the one in terms of being a whole and complete, the first simple one in each category, and the universal one described with precedence and postponement regarding everything enumerated in metaphysics. All of this offers no liberation, nor is it pure in terms of the perfection in which all three perfections reside; that is, the perfection that cuts through the imagination, verifies the Truth, and to which all respond. It is not as mentioned; it is possible, and its nature moves while it moves with it, and its bliss is likewise intended. It resembles the magnet in which there is a cycle for one who has understood and struck these words, then diverted them. 

This knowledge is in the mind before conceptualization and assent, not after them. The wise ignorant man is he who says: Life is a condition for intellect, intellect is a condition for knowledge, knowledge is a condition for action, action is a condition for virtue, virtue is a condition for happiness, happiness is a condition for goodness, goodness is a condition for perfection, and perfection is a condition for unity. And unity is the condition for the sought-after object. The sought-after object is that which is spoken of synonymously with things, univocally before them, by equivocation after them, by preference with them for it, by derivation within them, by removal from it, and by metaphor within them for it.

The virtuous, knowledgeable person places the condition in the place of the conditioned, and the wise successor makes the condition the conditioned without precedence or postponement. The wise, knowledgeable person does not find this because he is this.

The Wisdom of Imamate in the Word of Aaron

...by what is manifested, and the perfected knower—whether prophet, messenger, or heir to them—conceals it. He commanded them to withdraw from those images just as the messenger of the time withdrew from them, following the Messenger out of a desire for God’s love for them, according to His saying: "Say, if you love God, then follow me; God will love you" (Quran 3:31). He called [them] to a God who is sought and known in a general sense, yet He is not witnessed: "Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives vision" (Quran 6:103), due to His subtlety and His pervasion within the essences of things. Vision does not perceive Him, just as it does not perceive the spirits that govern their forms and apparent images. "And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted" (Quran 6:103); acquaintance is <term>dhawq</term> <gloss>direct tasting/experiential realization</gloss>, and tasting is a manifestation, and the manifestation is in images. Thus, images are necessary, and He is necessary; therefore, he who sees Him through his own desire must worship Him—if you understand—and to God is the intention of the path.

I say: He [Ibn Arabi], may God be pleased with him, mentioned the story of Aaron with Moses, and that Aaron, by virtue of the reality of divine mercy, was a prophet, for he was a mercy for his brother Moses. He mentioned that Aaron did not reject their worship of the calf; rather, he feared discord among the Children of Israel. He attributed to Moses, peace be upon him, the knowledge of the reality of the event, though he [Moses] did not confirm it until he burned the calf [137a]. He did not burn it out of a lack of knowledge that Lordship appears in the form of a calf, for he does not deny that. Rather, he acted upon it because it was an inanimate body or an animal, and both are subjected to man. Man has the right to judge over them as he pleases, because the rank of man is above the rank of what is other than him, as in the words of the Almighty: "And He has raised some of you above others in degrees" (Quran 6:165). Then he divided subjection into two types: compulsory subjection and relational subjection, and he provided examples for both.

Then he mentioned that nothing remains among things that has not been worshipped, either through an act of adoration or an act of relational state, and that the Almighty is the very essence of these things. This is because the Almighty decreed that none should be worshipped but Him, and this is explicitly stated in His saying: "And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him" (Quran 17:23), meaning He has judged, and there is no reversing His judgment. Thus, He is the One worshipped through many degrees, and that is why the Almighty is called the "Exalter of degrees" (Quran 40:15) and not "Exalter of the degree." He said that the greatest thing in which He is worshipped is the rank of desire: "Have you seen he who has taken as his god his own desire?" (Quran 45:23). Then he explained that no worshipper worships anything but his own desire, and his words are clear.

The sign of a plethora of blood is redness of the face, heaviness of the head and forehead when one inclines oneself, and the intensity of the throbbing; if the age, complexion, and season coincide with this, it will be stronger. The sign of gross windiness is pulling or stretching and much noise in the ear, with lightness of the head. The sign of a pustule or abscess which is called <term>al-malas</term> <gloss>abscess</gloss> is severe pain—it is called <term>al-malas</term>, and it is the strongest of all ear pains and the most dangerous, accompanied by pain in the whole forehead, head, and fever. The signs of cold or heat and vapor offending the ear from the outside are those which the patient reports, and because it happens after repetition. ### Of the noise and roaring of the ears follows. Chapter IV.

Noise and roaring of the ears, which is called <term>al-dawi</term> <gloss>buzzing</gloss> and <term>al-tanin</term> <gloss>ringing</gloss>, occurs from an intrinsic and extrinsic cause. The intrinsic occurs from eight causes, because it is either from gross wind existing in the head rising from the stomach, or from a gross humor, or from a hot humor existing in the head and rising from the stomach and the body, or from a weakness of hearing naturally or accidentally, or from some old illness, or from an illness happening before the arrival of a crisis from the collection of putrid humor or phlegm or congealed blood, or from that which in the time of health was in a state of clarity of hearing and lightness of head. The extrinsic cause is either from a plethora of much food and gross humor, or from exhaustion from purging or phlebotomy, or from a flow of blood or hunger from abstinence from food, or from much drinking of wine, or from much vomiting, or from much swimming in water or immersion in it, or from those things that enter the ear or animals entering it.

### Chapter on Explaining Parallax in the Zodiac Signs that are at Midheaven.

<margin>Chapter on Parallax</margin>
Chapter on Explaining Parallax in the Zodiac Signs that are at Midheaven. Know that for planets located at midheaven, if they are at the zenith <note>original: "سمت الرأس" <gloss>vertical point directly overhead</gloss></note>, they have no parallax <term>ikhtilaf al-manzar</term> <gloss>parallax</gloss>, because the zenith line passes through the center of the Earth and the center of the planet. If the planets are not at the zenith, their parallax occurs in longitude and latitude, and the parallax in longitude and latitude depends on the planet's distance from the zenith.

# A Section on Explaining Parallax <note>original: "اختلاف المنظر"</note> in the Zodiac Signs that are in the Midheaven.

<margin>Section on Parallax</margin>

A Section on Explaining Parallax in the Zodiac Signs that are in the Midheaven. Know that the planets <note>In medieval astronomy, the term "planets" (kawakib) includes the sun and moon.</note> that are in the midheaven, if they are at the zenith <term>samt al-ra's</term> <gloss>the point directly overhead</gloss>, have no parallax, because the line of the zenith passes through the center of the Earth and the center of the planet. If the planets are not at the zenith, their parallax occurs in longitude and latitude. The parallax in longitude and latitude depends on the distance of the planet from the zenith.

When the white one falls upon the name, it is known that he is blessed <note>referring to those destined for Paradise</note>. When the green one falls upon the name, it is known that he is wretched <note>referring to those destined for Hell</note>.

As for the place where he will die, it is said that God Almighty created an angel entrusted with every newborn, who is called the Angel of the Wombs. When a person is born, he stirs within the drop <note>of semen</note> that is in his mother’s womb from the soil of the earth upon which he will die. The servant then wanders wherever he wanders until he returns to the place of his earth <note>his birthplace or place of origin</note>, and there he dies. ### ( The Treatment of Iron )

Then they proceeded to the body of iron and found that the mineral salt attributed to it is table salt. They dissolved it in pure water, agitated it, and solidified it once, then calcined it and divided it into two halves. They dissolved one half in sea water of equal weight, then added to it an equal weight of oil, and cooked it, and it became a softening soap. Then, they coated the iron plates with some of this soap and rubbed the plate in the calcined, pulverized salt. They heated the plate and quenched it in some of this soap, repeating this seven times, for it becomes a pure iron that does not change throughout the ages, nor does the depth of the earth consume it. Then, they fashioned from it a tablet under the ascendant of Aries or Scorpio in the hour of the lord of the ascendant. Then, they engraved upon it the rising degree, that is, its image, then fumigated it with the incense of Mars. Then, they buried it in the eastern quarter, and from it arose the spirituality of Mars, and they are helpers in the likeness of the kings of the Turks and the Turkish assistants with various weapons. From it also arise calamities, terrifying fires, and the like.

### ( The Treatment of Gold )

Then they proceeded to the body of gold and found that the specific mineral salt is saltpeter. They dissolved it in an equal amount of water without filtration or calcination, because it is a pure spiritual substance. Then, they cooked it with oil, and it became a soap like snow. Then, they coated gold plates with some of the soap, rubbed them in the saltpeter, then heated them and quenched them in some of the oil, that is, the soap. Repeating this seven times, it became the talismanic gold of the people, which is pure from its origin, whereas the gold of the common people was not suitable for the talismans of the sages. Then, they fashioned from it a tablet under the ascendant of Leo and in the hour of the lord of that ascendant, which is the planet Sun. Then, they engraved upon it the image of the degree rising at that time in Leo, then fumigated it with the incense of that planet and buried it inside the treasure in the eastern quarter. From it arose the spirituality of the Sun, which is in the likeness of the kings of Persia and the kings of India, and from it appear terrifying beasts, deadly tigers, cats, eagles, and the like. This is not hidden from the knower. When the knower sees any obstacle, he knows which planet is dominating it, and after that, he can work against it to nullify it.

### ( The Treatment of Copper )

Then they took, after that, the body of copper and took the mineral salt suitable for it, which is vitriol salt. Regimen for maturatives: Warmth is such that it is suited to the warmth of the body, and a certain kind of moisture is added to them. Among these, in the first degrees, is an embrocation with warm water and an application of wheat flour, or barley and wheat, masticated with honey. In this, bread with pitch or wax and saffron and powdered frankincense, and pitch with rose oil, or hog's lard, or a plaster of mallow, mucilage, and flax seed. And again, a plaster of sweet, fat, rich figs, or with barley flour, or barley flour again, especially if there is placed in it hyssop or wild marjoram, or gathered with water in which they are boiled with a little salt, not in excess. And sometimes there is placed in it fat or oil, or two parts of glue from egg whites. And medicines composed of living-passis <note>likely a reference to a specific pharmaceutical preparation of bitumen or sulfur</note>, and tragacanth, and galbanum, and myrrh, and laudanum, and resin, and butter, and mastic, and hyssop, and the root of the wild cucumber, and the root of the dragon's lily. And the plaster of Galen with oil of kerua <note>castor oil</note> without wax, and especially when this plaster is dissolved in oil, and the plaster <term>didymoa</term> <gloss>a double or dual-purpose plaster</gloss> is made, and the plaster <term>basilicon</term> <gloss>royal or sovereign plaster</gloss>. And among the good things for this is a medicament of marchalite stone with ammoniac, which is placed on top until it falls off by itself.

Regimen for lancing when they are mature. L.xxix.

But you find an abscess of thick skin with maturation, for which its rupture is not expected. And there are veins and cords and nerves there. Then it is necessary that you lance it, because if you leave the sanies <note>thin, unhealthy pus</note>, it will rot and will corrode the skin and the fibers of the nerves. That will indeed be more severe when it is near the joints. And you must look for the place of the sanies with your lancing. And be careful that the lancing hole falls lower unless where it is not possible. And if that which is above the abscess is thick and you cut, then cut the hole only when you apply a poultice with that which is after it; and if it is thinned, then cut all of it lengthwise. And know that the place in which there is sanies is declared by touch, and when it is touched with a finger, you should observe specifically with the other fingers of the other hand whether something is expelled from it. And the place of the sanies appears from the declination of color toward whiteness, and then it is mature; and it declines toward redness. And sometimes the place of the sanies is declined toward redness and yellowness when the sanies is not good to sustain in touch without sight; however, sight is a helper. It is ordered, therefore, that in the incision you follow the natural lines of the ligaments, which are near the sanies, except in case of necessity; and in members diversified by the position of fibers in length and in the place of the ligament. For if you have followed that in the lancing of an abscess that is on the forehead, the ligament of the forehead skin will fall upon the face; rather, it is necessary that you diversify the ligament. In those indeed that are like the groin, it is necessary that you go with the ligament in the width of the skin. And when you have lanced the abscess and extracted what is in it, it is then necessary that you assist in gluing the skin with the flesh so that it does not rupture and harden and become such that it does not glue; whereby it becomes a passage that does not cease to be filled, and it is fed by the threads of the first abscess. And if it is necessary for you to use it, insert a probe, upon whose head there is rough cloth with which you cleanse the interior, then make it adhere and preserve it with a ligament according to what we will say about the ligaments of cavities and ulcers; it will be very convenient. And it is necessary that you observe in the lancing that which we have said about the conditions, where you lance in the more mature place and in a part more distant from veins, arteries, and cords.

<column-break/>

Antyllus says: If an abscess is in the head, then its incision is made wide; and if it happens in the nose, we will lance it equal to the quantity of the length of the nose. And if it is near the eye, we will lance it with a lancing of a thread for the head of the new moon, and we will make the curvature downward. If however it happens in the jaw, we will cut it with an equal incision, when the composition of this place is equal, and that is known from the bodies of the fenu <note>likely referring to the canonical body of medical knowledge or the preceding books</note>. But after the ear, we lance all those of the groin in length. He says: and if it is near the thighs, we will lance it with a round lancing; and a round lancing is that which grasps with its grasp the length of the body, something of its width. He says: when this place is not lanced round, it is possible that matters gather in it and become fistulas. And also, that which is near the anus is lanced, because of the place of humidity that gathers in it. And in the side and ribs, it is lanced by opening; in the testicle and member, however, in an equal manner. He says: and let us be ready always so that the section follows the figure of the place as much as we can upon it. The sides, however, and the supports are cut in length, and preserve that you do not injure the nerves. And know that the lancing is diversified according to the places: for when it is the eye, then its length is wide according to the position of the eye; and in the nose, it is according to the length of the nose; and in the jaw, it is according to the length of the jaw; and near the ear, it is cut equally, when the position of this place is equal, and that is known from the bodies of the fenu. After the ear, however, it is lanced equally; in the arms and legs and thigh and member, it is all made equal in length. And it is done in the muscles and in the back; in the groins and the groin area, you will prepare for the lancing, taking from the width also so that a sinus may not be made in it that becomes a fistula. And it is done in that which is near the anus, take from the width also so that a sinus may not result and become a fistula; and the testicles and member are equal and in length; in the side and ribs, take in the width also so that it is transverse, because the position of the ribs is such, and the flesh that is upon them. He says: consider always the position of the flesh and the fibers of the muscles, because we are not ready except for this, that we lance with imitation of the place so that no sinus may result and the place of flesh-growth becomes good, not thick. And do in all your study that you do not cut an artery, nor a great vein, or nerve, or the fibers of the muscle, and the lancing is made according to the magnitude of the abscess. But if it is small and what is in it runs from one place, then cut it in one place; and if it is large, then lance it from the beginning, then insert your index finger of the left hand into it and lance it where the head arrives, and then insert it also into the opening, and according to this until you come upon it. And if the abscess has a sufficient place from which it is possible for what is in it to exit, we will lance it in that place; and if it is round or has a figure so that what is in it does not exit by one lancing, we will lance it in its interior part in two places or three, according to the quantity that you know, because everything that gathers in it runs in an hour. He says: let there not be an abscess [on] a puncture, or a noble member, or a member near a bone, or in the perineum, [lest] we hasten in the lancing; and sometimes we confirm its maturation so that it does not corrupt any of these members. I say therefore this is the regimen when we do not find an excuse for lancing. If, however, we hope that it may rupture through a poultice, we will not lance, and similarly if we hope that it may erupt through medicines causing eruption; perhaps, indeed, we find in medicines causing eruption that they stand in the place of lancing. And very often the skin is lanced by some lancing, or something is taken from it, afterward eruptions are placed upon it so that a lancing is made for it.
